 Meta Begins Listing 3D Movies On Quest, Could Become A Horizon+ Benefit
 ,  
  &  
 Luna 
 Today
 A limited selection of 3D movies has begun appearing in the TV app on Quest headsets, and datamining suggests that 3D movies may become a benefit of the Meta Horizon+ subscription service.
 At Meta Connect 2026 in September, alongside the reveal of Meta VR Glasses , the company announced that Quest owners in the US would be able to rent or buy "hundreds" of movies in late 2026. The company said that this catalog will eventually expand to "thousands" of titles available internationally by the time Meta VR Glasses launch in 2027.
 Now, some Quest 3 and 3S owners have spotted a limited selection of 3D movies in the TV app, while Meta has also added new support articles describing the ability to rent or buy media.
 The movies listed so far appear to consist primarily of Disney-owned content. Notably, they can be purchased directly through the Meta Horizon Store without an active Disney+ subscription.
 Separately, the Disney+ app is set to receive its own overhaul on the platform this month, bringing a new spatial UI, support for 3D media, and several of the immersive environments also available in the Disney+ app for visionOS on Apple Vision Pro.
 Meta Expands SDKs To Boost Spatial Apps On Quest & VR Glasses, Including NBA, Disney+ Meta announced several new SDKs and features to enhance spatial apps on Quest and Meta VR Glasses, alongside major spatial updates for the NBA and Disney+ apps. UploadVR Luna Additionally, a page discovered in the TV app by user Nikita and shared by dataminer and programmer Nori suggests that Meta may begin offering 3D movies as part of the Horizon+ subscription service. The page also suggests that the service may be rebranded as Meta VR+.
 Such a rebrand would fit with the company's broader efforts to separate Horizon Worlds and related branding from the Quest platform, which began earlier this year .
 If you're unfamiliar, Meta Horizon+ is the company's $8/month (or $60/year) subscription service for its VR devices. Subscribers get access to a Games Catalog of around 50 major VR titles, as well as an Indie Catalog of around 50 smaller titles, for a total of around 100 games.
 Subscribers are also offered two specific games each month, pre-selected by Meta. Redeeming them lets you play those games while your subscription is active. If you cancel, you can regain access to previously redeemed games by resubscribing.
 In February 2026, Meta reported that the subscription service had crossed 1 million "active subscribers" in 2025 . In July, the company also added a starter edition of Xbox Game Pass to Horizon+, giving subscribers access to 50+ games and 10 hours of cloud gaming each month. More recently, the service has started regularly offering subscribers exclusive game discounts and free add-ons for games.
 Quest's Horizon+ Subscription Adds 10 Hours Of Xbox Cloud Gaming Quest's Horizon+ subscription added 10 monthly hours of flatscreen cloud streaming for 58 Xbox titles, furthering Meta's partnership with Microsoft. UploadVR David Heaney Adding 3D movies to Horizon+ would align with the media focus of Meta VR Glasses and recent Horizon OS updates , as well as the strategy outlined by Meta Director of Games Chris Pruett  at GDC in March.
 Pruett stated that the company expects "more Mainstream Adults to enter VR through media consumption first, then discover games once they are in-headset" over the next couple of years. He described the demographic as people who "are mid-core, love Meta Horizon+, and probably play seated without controllers".
